title: Pointed torsor descent identifies trivialized lines with characters
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be a finite commutative $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $X,Y$ be $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $q:X\to Y$ be a finite flat surjective morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] with a right $G$-action for which
$$X\times_kG\longrightarrow X\times_YX,\qquad (x,g)\longmapsto(x,xg)$$
is an isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix $x_0\in X(k)$ and put $y_0=q(x_0)$. Assume that for every $k$-scheme $S$ the structure map induces an isomorphism $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X\times_kS,\mathcal O)$. For every $k$-scheme $T$, let $K_q(T)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(L,r)$, where $L$ is an invertible module on $Y_T$ [def-sc-invertible-module], $r:y_{0,T}^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_T$ is a specified rigidification, and $q_T^*L$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{X_T}$ by an isomorphism restricting to $r$ along $x_{0,T}$. All pullbacks are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. Tensor product gives $K_q(T)$ a group [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There are bijections of groups, natural in $T$,
$$K_q(T)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{T\text{-grp}}(G_T,\mathbf G_{m,T}),$$
with $\mathbf G_m$ as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. The normalized trivialization of $q_T^*L$ is unique. Under the displayed torsor isomorphism, its descent isomorphism on $X_T\times_{Y_T}X_T$ is multiplication by the pullback of the corresponding character along $X_T\times_TG_T\to G_T$. Conversely, descent of the trivial line with this multiplier produces $(L,r)$. Fix throughout the convention that this multiplier is the character rather than its inverse. These descriptions commute with arbitrary base change in $T$, including nonreduced $T$.

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent, and lemma-finite-locally-free-descends. Pointed character classification is an agent-derived torsor specialization: the descent multiplier is independent of X by the universal global-functions hypothesis; the cocycle identity is the character law.

proof.text: The singleton $\{q:X\to Y\}$ is an fpqc covering. Indeed, $q$ is flat by hypothesis; over an affine open $V\subseteq Y$, finiteness says that $q^{-1}(V)$ is affine, and surjectivity says its image is all of $V$. This is exactly the affine-open condition in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] to $Y_T\to Y$: $\{q_T:X_T\to Y_T\}$ is fpqc for every $T$, with no reducedness or finiteness assumption on $T$.

proof.text: Fix $(L,r)\in K_q(T)$ and an allowed trivialization $\tau:q_T^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{X_T}$. Any two such trivializations differ by an $\mathcal O_{X_T}$-linear automorphism of $\mathcal O_{X_T}$. Such an automorphism is multiplication by the global unit which is its value on $1$: on an open $U$, linearity sends $f$ to $f\,a|_U$, and its inverse gives $a^{-1}$. The hypothesis with $S=T$ says that $a$ is the pullback of a unique unit $v\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$. Since both trivializations restrict to $r$ along $x_{0,T}$, $v=1$. Thus $\tau$ is unique. Here the pullback identifications along $q_Tx_{0,T}=y_{0,T}$ are those of [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent; Tag 05B2, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends; agent-derived pointed torsor calculation

proof.text: Let $p_1,p_2:X_T\times_{Y_T}X_T\to X_T$ be the projections. The equality $q_Tp_1=q_Tp_2$ gives the canonical isomorphism $c:p_1^*q_T^*L\to p_2^*q_T^*L$, with its cocycle identity by composition of these identifications [def-pc-module-pullback]. In the frames $p_i^*\tau$, put $d=(p_2^*\tau)c(p_1^*\tau)^{-1}$. As in step 2, this is multiplication by a global unit. Pull it through the assumed torsor isomorphism $(x,g)\mapsto(x,xg)$ to a unit $a$ on $X_T\times_TG_T=X\times_kG_T$. Apply the universal global-functions hypothesis with the $k$-scheme $S=G_T$: there is a unique $b\in\Gamma(G_T,\mathcal O_{G_T})^\times$ with $a=\operatorname{pr}_{G_T}^*b$. Explicitly $b=(x_0,\mathrm{id})^*a$. This establishes independence of $X$ as a scheme-theoretic equality, not just on geometric points.

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent; Tag 05B2, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends; agent-derived pointed torsor calculation

proof.text:
The torsor isomorphism identifies the triple overlap with $X_T\times_TG_T\times_TG_T$, by $(x,g,h)\mapsto(x,xg,xgh)$. Thus the cocycle identity is
$$a(x,gh)=a(xg,h)a(x,g).$$
Substitution of $a=\operatorname{pr}_{G_T}^*b$ and restriction along the section $x_0$ give $m^*b=\operatorname{pr}_2^*b\,\operatorname{pr}_1^*b$ on $G_T\times_TG_T$. On the identity section this gives $e^*b=(e^*b)^2$, so $e^*b=1$ since it is a unit; applying the inverse gives $i^*b=b^{-1}$. The unit $b$ defines a $T$-morphism $\chi:G_T\to\mathbf G_{m,T}$ [def-sc-gm-ga]: on affine opens the coordinate map sends $t$ to $b$ and $t^{-1}$ to $b^{-1}$, and the maps agree on overlaps [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The displayed identities say exactly that this morphism respects the group operations [def-sc-group-scheme]. This fixes the convention $d=\chi$, with no inverse inserted.

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent; Tag 05B2, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends; agent-derived pointed torsor calculation

proof.text: Conversely, for a $T$-group homomorphism $\chi:G_T\to\mathbf G_{m,T}$, give $\mathcal O_{X_T}$ the overlap isomorphism which, under $(x,g)\mapsto(x,xg)$, multiplies by $\chi(g)$. The character law yields $\chi(gh)=\chi(h)\chi(g)$, precisely the cocycle equation of step 4; $\chi(e)=1$ gives the diagonal identity. Apply the effective descent and rank-one assertions of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] to the fpqc covering in step 1. They give an invertible module $L$ on $Y_T$ and a compatible isomorphism $\tau:q_T^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{X_T}$. Pulling $\tau$ back along $x_{0,T}$ defines $r:y_{0,T}^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_T$. Thus $(L,r)\in K_q(T)$, and step 2 makes this $\tau$ the normalized trivialization. The descended line is invertible because the descent datum is rank one, exactly the case expressly included in the cited statement.

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent; Tag 05B2, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends; agent-derived pointed torsor calculation

proof.text: These constructions give inverse maps on isomorphism classes. Starting with a character, step 5 uses its very multiplier, so steps 3--4 recover that character. Starting with $(L,r)$, its normalized frame identifies its canonical descent datum with the one constructed from its character. Full faithfulness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] descends the identity of these framed data to a unique isomorphism of the descended lines; restricting its compatibility with the frames along $x_{0,T}$ proves that it respects $r$. Also, an isomorphism of rigidified lines carries their normalized frames to one another by step 2, so it gives the same multiplier. Different choices of an effective descent in step 5 are related by the same uniquely descended frame-compatible isomorphism. This proves well-definedness and bijectivity without choosing preferred representatives.

source.place: Tag 023T, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent; Tag 05B2, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends; agent-derived pointed torsor calculation

proof.text: Tensor product gives the asserted groups. Let $(L_1,r_1),(L_2,r_2)\in K_q(T)$ with normalized frames $\tau_1,\tau_2$ and characters $\chi_1,\chi_2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (1), $L_1\otimes L_2$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and by its clause (2) the pullback isomorphisms $q_T^*(L_1\otimes L_2)\cong q_T^*L_1\otimes q_T^*L_2$ and $y_{0,T}^*(L_1\otimes L_2)\cong y_{0,T}^*L_1\otimes y_{0,T}^*L_2$ send $f^*(s\otimes t)$ to $f^*s\otimes f^*t$ and are compatible with the composition isomorphisms $x_{0,T}^*q_T^*\cong y_{0,T}^*$ and $p_i^*q_T^*\cong(q_Tp_i)^*$. Hence $\tau_1\otimes\tau_2$ is a trivialization of $q_T^*(L_1\otimes L_2)$ restricting to $r_1\otimes r_2$, so $(L_1\otimes L_2,r_1\otimes r_2)\in K_q(T)$ and, by step 2, $\tau_1\otimes\tau_2$ is its normalized frame. Computing on local generators, the canonical descent isomorphism of $q_T^*(L_1\otimes L_2)$ is the tensor product of those of $q_T^*L_1$ and $q_T^*L_2$, so in the frame $\tau_1\otimes\tau_2$ its scalar is $\chi_1(g)\chi_2(g)$, since $(u e_1)\otimes(v e_2)=uv(e_1\otimes e_2)$. The class of $(\mathcal O_{Y_T},\mathrm{id})$, with frame the canonical $q_T^*\mathcal O_{Y_T}\cong\mathcal O_{X_T}$, has scalar $1$. Tensor associativity and the symmetry of clause (2) are isomorphisms that act on pure tensors by reassociation and swap, so they respect the tensored rigidifications; thus tensor product is an associative commutative operation with unit on $K_q(T)$, and the map to characters of step 6 is multiplicative. Inverses: by step 6 there is a class $(L',r')$ with character $\chi^{-1}$; then $(L\otimes L',r\otimes r')$ has character $1$, which is also the character of $(\mathcal O_{Y_T},\mathrm{id})$, so the two are isomorphic by the injectivity in step 6. Hence $K_q(T)$ is a group and the bijection of step 6 is a group isomorphism.

proof.text: For any $f:T'\to T$, pull back a rigidified line along $Y_{T'}\to Y_T$, together with its rigidification and its normalized frame; the pullback is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (1). Composition of tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback] shows that the resulting frame restricts to the pulled-back rigidification, hence it is the unique normalized frame over $T'$. Pullback of multiplication by $b$ is multiplication by its pulled-back unit, so its character is $\chi_{T'}$. Conversely, pulling back the compatible descent isomorphism of step 5 gives the datum with multiplier $\chi_{T'}$. Full faithfulness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent], applied to the fpqc covering over $T'$ of step 1, identifies it with the descent constructed over $T'$, preserving the frames and therefore the rigidifications. All equalities used were identities of sections or tensor pullbacks on the full schemes; they remain valid for arbitrary, including nonreduced and empty, $T'$ without any flatness assumption on $f$.
